When one categorical factor lacks two qualifying levels, all of that factor's rows remain while the factor is omitted, allowing its effects to confound coefficients advertised as adjusted model/tool effects.
The unrestricted number of categorical levels can make the normal-equation implementation quadratic in memory and cubic in work without an input budget or probe.

findings.title: Raw transcript content can cross the LLM boundary without secret redaction
findings.what: The formatter copies assistant text and serialized tool-use inputs into the judge prompt verbatim. Tool inputs and transcript prose can contain tokens, environment values, file contents, or other ~/.claude-derived secrets. This module neither redacts them nor conveys an enforceable classification preventing use of the subscription OAuth credential, so its correctness depends entirely on an out-of-band caller convention.
findings.fix: Apply a centralized transcript-egress sanitizer before constructing the prompt and require the injected judge interface to accept an explicit data-classification/credential-policy value that rejects subscription OAuth for ~/.claude-derived content.
findings.acceptance: A test transcript containing representative API keys, authorization headers, environment secrets, and tool-read content reaches a capturing judge only in redacted form; a subscription-OAuth-backed judge rejects the classified request before network dispatch.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that both text blocks and compacted tool inputs are copied into `transcript`, then interpolated unchanged into `judge({user})`; no sanitizer or credential-policy argument exists in the cited path.

findings.title: Substring server matching suppresses unrelated MCP adoption gaps
findings.what: Coverage uses substring containment in either direction. An installed ID such as `webhook` therefore matches the known server name `web`, and an ID such as `github-backup` matches `github`, even when those servers do not provide the mapped capability. `detectCapabilityGaps` then drops an evidence-backed gap as already covered.
findings.fix: Normalize server IDs into explicit namespace/name tokens and compare exact known aliases, or carry authoritative capability IDs from configuration instead of inferring coverage by arbitrary substring.
findings.acceptance: Add cases showing that `claude_ai_GitHub` still covers GitHub, while unrelated IDs such as `webhook`, `github-backup`, and `browserless-metrics` do not suppress their respective capability gaps unless explicitly registered as aliases.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read the matcher and drop branch and confirmed the concrete reproduction: `nameMatches('webhook','web')` is true, causing `isCovered` to remove a `web-fetch` candidate.

findings.title: Omitted thin factor remains in the sample and can confound advertised adjusted effects
findings.what: `chooseLevels` returns null when a factor has fewer than two qualifying levels. The corresponding `modelOk` or `toolOk` then returns true for every row, but no column for that factor is added. If the other factor varies, the fit proceeds and reports its coefficients as adjusted model/tool effects even though variation in the omitted factor remains in the sample. Correlation between the omitted factor and a retained factor can therefore create a false edge.
findings.fix: Distinguish a constant factor from a factor containing unmodeled thin levels. When a factor cannot be contrasted, retain only its single qualifying reference level (or reject the fit); never keep heterogeneous levels while omitting the factor.
findings.acceptance: Construct rows where model has one qualifying level plus a thin second level perfectly correlated with a tool level. The audit must either exclude the thin-model rows or return insufficient, and must not report the confounded tool level as an adjusted edge.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that null factor metadata makes the filter unconditional (`!modelLevels`/`!toolLevels`) and that the resulting output is explicitly described as adjusted after controlling for difficulty; no later omitted-factor check exists.

findings.title: Unbounded categorical cardinality makes the regression cubic
findings.what: Every level with only three rows can add a design column, so k grows linearly with session count. Building X'X costs O(n*k^2), storing and augmenting the matrix costs O(k^2), and Gauss-Jordan inversion costs O(k^3). No maximum row/level/term budget or runtime probe bounds this server endpoint.
findings.fix: Cap modeled levels/terms using deterministic support ranking, reject oversized designs before allocation, and record fit duration, row count, and term count against an explicit endpoint budget. A numerically stable solver that avoids materializing an inverse would further reduce risk.
findings.acceptance: A high-cardinality input at the documented maximum is either rejected as insufficient before allocating the k-by-2k augmented matrix or completes within the declared latency and memory budget; telemetry exposes rows, terms, duration, and rejection reason.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-derived the loops: X'X iterates k² pairs over n rows and elimination iterates k pivots over k rows and 2k columns. Because minPerCell=3 is the only cardinality constraint, k remains O(n).
